name: Pale Hortense Violet
lede: Pale Hortense Violet is a pale pink-violet named, like the garden hydrangea Hortensia, for a flower rather than a dye or a place.

sections.title: A flower, not a pigment
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color standards place this swatch on plate XI, hue 61, tone f [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, citing the same plate, classes it in block 221 and lists three names for the identical swatch: Bouquet Orchid, Cosmos Pink and Orchid Lane [1]. All four names point to flowers, not to any dye or mineral, which is why ColorHub's tagging files it under nature rather than pigment [1]. The flower in the headline name is Hortensia, the garden hydrangea, whose own blooms range from blue to this pale pink-violet depending on the soil's acidity [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[light-orchid]], [[light-lavender]] and [[pale-violet]], at 2.8, [[orchid]], [[lavender]] and [[pink]] sit in the same pale-violet family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color within CIEDE2000 distance 6 of Pale Hortense Violet covering even 5 percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole, and it is consistent with the color's history: a pale, saturated pink-violet like this is easier to print or dye than to mix and apply as a stable paint [2]. The closest things a painter could actually reach are [[orchid]] and [[lavender]] [1].
